anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level statements or transaction flows demand more data, rows, or time than the business case requires.
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Table structures, partitioning, and index choices are mis-aligned with access patterns, forcing inefficient access paths even for well-written queries.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine runtime parameters (memory, logging, parallelism, checkpoints, etc.) are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity and workload characteristics.

When all three conditions coexist, the database is simultaneously stressed by excessive logical work, sub-optimal physical access paths, and ill-sized runtime resources. Observable symptoms include: 
• Extremely long and erratic statement latencies, with the same queries dominating slow-query logs and holding locks far beyond normal durations.
• Execution plans showing table or index scans, repeated key lookups, and spilled sorts/hash operations, accompanied by high physical I/O despite low buffer-pool hit ratios.
• Wait-event patterns that oscillate between I/O starvation and artificial throttling (e.g., small dirty-page checkpoints, excessive log flush waits, memory pressure evictions) even though hardware metrics show unused capacity.
• Sudden throughput collapses or timeouts under peak load as bloated transactions interact with write-amplified indexes and mis-sized memory/worker limits, causing lock escalation, checkpoint storms, and cache thrashing.

Causal chain: Inefficient SQL logic expands the data that must be read, joined, sorted, or updated. Because the schema lacks appropriate indexes or partitions, those inflated requests translate into large sequential or random scans, excessive row fetches, and heavier undo/redo generation. The escalated I/O, memory, and concurrency demands collide with poorly chosen configuration parameters—such as undersized buffer pools, over-aggressive work-memory, or misaligned checkpoint intervals—preventing the engine from absorbing the extra load. The configuration shortfalls amplify the latency introduced by design flaws, while the workload’s bloated access patterns hinder background maintenance tasks tuned for lower volumes, creating feedback loops of backlog, contention, and unpredictable performance degradation. Together, the three root causes reinforce one another, masking individual symptoms and driving the database into chronic instability until each layer is addressed in concert.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
